key_insight: Confidence-based retrieval routing becomes nearly random on specialist biomedical questions, precisely where retrieval improves accuracy most.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical QA systems facing unfamiliar specialist questions, always retrieving supporting literature may be more reliable than using model confidence to decide when to retrieve.
method: Evaluated adaptive retrieval across three biomedical QA benchmarks of increasing difficulty and multiple model sizes.
Compared five uncertainty signals, including token probabilities, sampling consistency, and verbalized confidence.
Tested five post-hoc calibration correction strategies.
evidence_signal: Confidence AUROC was 0.78–0.89 on standard exam questions but 0.506 on specialist questions, where retrieval improved accuracy by 11.2%; calibration corrections reached only 0.507 AUROC.
watch_item: Benchmark results do not establish clinical safety; retrieval quality and routing reliability require validation in the intended deployment setting.
paper_title: Confidence-Based Adaptive Retrieval Fails Where It Matters Most: A Paradox in Biomedical Question Answering
